items.followUp: Define data backup and explain why it is important.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that security protects a computer system or its data from unauthorized access or threats.
rubric.description: Defines security as protection from unauthorized access or threats.
rubric.how: Look for protection and an idea such as unauthorized access, threats, or attacks.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that maintenance keeps a computer or its components in good working condition.
rubric.description: Defines maintenance as keeping a computer in good working condition.
rubric.how: Look for maintaining or restoring the computer's working condition, for example through updates or repairs.

modelAnswer: Security means protecting a computer system and its data from unauthorized access, damage, or threats.
Maintenance means taking care of a computer system to keep it in good working condition, for example by updating or repairing it.

rubric.why: Award one mark for stating that system software is software that manages or controls the computer's hardware or basic operations.
rubric.description: Identifies system software as software that manages or controls the computer system.
rubric.how: Look for software/program and a management or control role.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that system software provides a platform or environment for application software to run.
rubric.description: Explains that system software supports application software.
rubric.how: Look for a platform or environment that lets applications run.

modelAnswer: System software is a set of programs that manages and controls a computer's hardware and basic operations.
It also provides a platform on which application software can run.

items.followUp: What is a router, and what does it do in a network?

rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying a switch as a network device that connects devices on a network.
rubric.description: Identifies a switch as a device that connects network devices.
rubric.how: Look for a device and the idea of connecting computers or other devices.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that a switch forwards data to its intended device or port.
rubric.description: Explains that a switch directs data to its intended destination.
rubric.how: Look for forwarding or sending data to the correct device or destination.

modelAnswer: A switch is a network device that connects computers and other devices in a local area network (LAN).
It forwards data to the intended device on the network.

items.followUp: Explain abstraction and give one example of irrelevant detail it can leave out.

rubric.why: Award one mark for saying that abstraction focuses on the important or relevant features of a problem.
rubric.description: States that abstraction focuses on important features.
rubric.how: Look for focusing on important, essential, or relevant information.

rubric.why: Award one mark for saying that abstraction ignores or removes irrelevant or unnecessary details.
rubric.description: States that abstraction leaves out irrelevant details.
rubric.how: Look for ignoring, omitting, or removing unnecessary information.

modelAnswer: Abstraction is the process of focusing on the important features of a problem.
It leaves out irrelevant or unnecessary details to make the problem easier to understand.

items.followUp: What is an algorithm, and how can pseudocode help before programming?

rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying pseudocode as a way to express or represent the steps of an algorithm.
rubric.description: Explains that pseudocode represents an algorithm's steps.
rubric.how: Look for pseudocode and steps or an algorithm.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that pseudocode helps plan or check a solution before writing program code.
rubric.description: Explains its use in planning a program before coding.
rubric.how: Look for planning or designing a solution before coding or programming.

modelAnswer: Pseudocode expresses the steps of an algorithm in simple, human-readable language.
It helps plan and check the logic of a solution before writing program code.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <title> tag in an HTML document?

rubric.why: Award one mark for stating that the head section contains information or metadata about the HTML document.
rubric.description: States that the head contains document information or metadata.
rubric.how: Look for metadata, information, or settings associated with the document.

rubric.why: Award one mark for naming something placed in the head, such as the page title, stylesheet link, or script reference.
rubric.description: Gives a valid example of content placed inside the head.
rubric.how: Look for a page title, stylesheet link, script, or similar document resource.

modelAnswer: The <head> tag contains information (metadata) about an HTML document that is not displayed as the page's main content.
It can contain the page title, links to stylesheets, and references to scripts.

items.followUp: What does HTML do in a web page?

rubric.why: Award one mark for expanding CSS as Cascading Style Sheets or identifying it as a stylesheet language.
rubric.description: Gives the name or type of CSS.
rubric.how: Look for Cascading Style Sheets or stylesheet language.

rubric.why: Award one mark for explaining that CSS controls a web page's appearance, formatting, or layout.
rubric.description: Explains that CSS styles the presentation of web pages.
rubric.how: Look for styling, formatting, appearance, or layout of a web page.

modelAnswer: CSS stands for Cascading Style Sheets.
It is a stylesheet language used to control the appearance, formatting, and layout of web pages.

items.followUp: Define quantitative data and give one example.

rubric.why: Award one mark for identifying qualitative data as descriptive information about qualities or characteristics.
rubric.description: Defines qualitative data as descriptive information about qualities or characteristics.
rubric.how: Look for descriptive information, qualities, characteristics, or categories.

rubric.why: Award one mark for stating that qualitative data is non-numerical or giving a valid categorical example.
rubric.description: Distinguishes qualitative data from numerical data or provides an appropriate example.
rubric.how: Look for non-numerical data or an example such as colour, type, or opinion.

modelAnswer: Qualitative data is descriptive, non-numerical information about qualities or characteristics.
Examples include colour, type of computer, and a person's opinion.
